messages:
alex: quick q — for the internal fronting layer (user-facing -> platform) are we leaning towards a thin transport adapter per-service or a central edge proxy? thinking about quotas, telemetry correlation, rollout UX.

maria: +1 to listing pros/cons. Adapter = per-service quotas + exact telemetry (no polyglot decoding) but more client work. Edge proxy = single enforcement plane, easier global quotas, but harder to attach request-level model/cache metadata.

sam: agreed. ops perspective: central proxy makes rate-limiting simpler but becomes a single scaling surface. also we lose some per-model latency visibility unless we propagate extra headers (x-rw-model, x-rw-batch-size)

jordan: proto-first here: gRPC + x-proto headers give typed metadata. REST/json forces ad-hoc key naming. Not a hill to die on though.

evan: product/console angle: rollout UX matters — can we do canary traffic splits by model version if we go central? dashboard should show per-route A/B metrics.

maria: we can if proxy supports weighted routing and tags traces. but then logs need to include model id + shard id. sample header idea:
```
X-RW-Model: redwood/gpt-4o-7b
X-RW-Variant: q4_0
X-RW-Route: chat.generate
```

sam: +1 header approach. For quotas we'd want token-cost-in-request header so proxy can decrement tokens. but that requires clients to estimate tokens or runtime to report downstream.

alex: is it realistic for adapter model runtimes to push token-cost back upstream synchronously? feels hairy.

evan: console could show provisional vs final cost, maybe charge provisional upfront and reconcile. UX ok with that?

jordan: we keep thinking about typed contracts. If we use protobufs we can carry structured quota metadata as a message field instead of headers. less brittle.

maria: tradeoffs: protobuf = faster, compact, easier to enforce schema. but adds friction for javascript-first teams. we have SDKs though.

sam: operational failure modes: proxy misconfig can kill all tenants. adapter lets teams opt-in so blast radius smaller.

alex: propose hybrid: central proxy for ingress + global quotas + telemetry aggregation, with per-service adapter layer that annotates requests with authoritative metadata (model id, token-count). proxy acts as gatekeeper but trusts adapter metadata signed via HMAC header.

evan: that sounds promising. signed metadata solves client trust issues. dashboard calls out whether metadata is proxy-verified.

jordan: implementation sketch:
```
client -> proxy (auth+narrow bw checks) -> sidecar adapter (annotate/sign) -> service runtime
```
Or reverse the sign order: adapter signs before proxy so proxy can verify and enforce.

sam: signature before proxy means adapter must be reachable from client. for private deployments that's fine but hosted api clients hit proxy first.

maria: final notes: we need tracing correlation id across all hops and a schema for telemetry fields. propose RFC doc with examples and rollout plan.

alex: cool. I'll draft RFC with hybrid design + header/proto schemas + rollout plan + consoles metrics list. tagging @sam @maria @jordan @evan for review. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: platform-proxy v1.12 -> canary (5%) at 2026-03-20T16:20:00Z

sam: saw canary note. let's queue RFC review before wide rollout.

maria: acked. will add telemetry tests.

alex: thanks everyone.
